prompt: An exec pushes hard to skip the security review. Having heard him out, the engineer calmly repeats that the data shows real risk and the review takes two days.
tells: calmly repeats that the data shows real risk
why: If your reasons still stand, restate them calmly.
trap: She doesn't give in, and she isn't restating his case.

prompt: After listening to every objection, a lead says, 'I've heard the concerns and I still think we need the migration first. Here's why, again, briefly.'
tells: 'I've heard the concerns and I still think
trap: There's no new test proposed; it's restating a view.

prompt: A manager asks an engineer to cut her estimate from six weeks to three. She explains the risky parts again and keeps the six-week estimate.
why: Don't drop an honest estimate under pressure.
trap: She's not uncovering needs; she's standing by her estimate.

prompt: In a system design interview, the interviewer argues for a single database. The candidate considers it, then says the write volume still needs sharding and shows the numbers.
tells: then says the write volume still needs sharding and shows the numbers
why: Interviewers often test whether you'll defend a sound choice.
trap: Folding to sound agreeable isn't the goal when the numbers hold.

prompt: A director plays devil's advocate for the fourth time. The analyst says, 'I understand the objection; the three customer interviews still point the same way.'
tells: the three customer interviews still point the same way
why: Hold a well-supported position under pressure.
trap: She acknowledges the objection but doesn't fold.

prompt: In an interview, a candidate describes refusing to sign off on a release despite pressure from sales, after rechecking that the bug was real.
tells: refusing to sign off on a release despite pressure from sales
why: Stand firm when you've checked and still believe it.
trap: The pressure is the cue, and they don't give in.
